title: Canonical-braid interface composition $(n_{pp}, n_{pn}, n_{nn})$ for atom $(Z, N)$ in pppnnn ordering
html:
Definition. Canonical-braid interface composition (n_{pp}, n_{pn}, n_{nn}) for atom (Z, N) in pppnnn ordering

Definition (canonical-braid interface composition). Let \beta(Z, N) \in H_{3A}(q) be the canonical atomic braid in standard pppnnn ordering. The A - 1 inter-nucleon interface generators \sigma_{3k + 2} are classified by the flavour pair they bridge:

See Table 1.

The (\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n}) entry \sigma - h/2 is the uniform bar-invariant average, i.e. the \delta = 0 convention. The colour-tube-weighted form \sigma - h(1/2 - \delta/4), with \delta the substrate flavour split of prop:flavor-split-substrate, is the canonical interface factor; the two differ by h\delta/4. The composition counts below are unaffected, depending only on which pairs occur and not on the content assigned to each generator.

The composition (n_{pp}, n_{pn}, n_{nn}) counts these three types. Under canonical ordering, the closed forms are:

n_{pp} = \max(0, Z - 1), \quad
n_{nn} = \max(0, N - 1), \quad
n_{pn} = \begin{cases} 1 & Z \geq 1, N \geq 1 \\ 0 & \text{else}\end{cases}

with total count summing to A - 1.

See Table 2.

The asymmetric counts (n_{pp}, n_{nn}) encode the Z \leftrightarrow N asymmetry directly. Alternative orderings produce different interface compositions. The canonical formalism fixes the pppnnn ordering.

The interface asymmetry isolates the {}^{3}He anomaly. A linear fit across the interfaces evaluates the 4-atom set, requiring evaluation against larger A to verify structural predictions.
